context.objective: Document how we carry out Supplier statement reconciliation, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: What starts this work?
Every Monday at 9:00 the AP clerk downloads the supplier statements that arrived in the shared mailbox ap-statements during the previous week.
What does the AP clerk do with the statements after downloading them?
The clerk saves each statement PDF into the folder Statements/YYYY-WW on the shared drive.
What records does the clerk compare each statement against?

The clerk exports the open-items report for that supplier from our ledger system, Ledgerline, and compares the statement lines with those open items in the workbook Statement Rec Template, one tab per supplier.
How are differences between a statement line and an open item handled?
If the total difference for a supplier is under 50 pounds it is noted and ignored. For larger differences the clerk classifies each one as missing invoice, payment in transit, duplicate, or disputed.
What does the clerk do after classifying a larger difference?

It depends on the class. For a missing invoice the clerk emails the supplier the same day asking for a copy and logs it in the Rec Log sheet. For a duplicate the clerk emails me the same day. A payment in transit needs no action and is just noted. A disputed item goes to the buyer who placed the order.
What does the buyer do with a disputed item after it is referred to them?
The buyer has 5 business days to reply to the dispute. If they do not, I chase them once, and after that the item goes to the finance manager.
What does the finance manager do when the disputed item is escalated to them?
The finance manager, Dana Whitlock, decides the outcome of the dispute with the buyer and the supplier, and tells me and the clerk so the item can be resolved in Ledgerline and the Rec Log.
What does the clerk change in Ledgerline to resolve a disputed item?

The clerk does not change anything in Ledgerline for a dispute itself. If the finance manager decides the supplier is right, nothing changes. If we are right, the clerk asks the supplier for a credit note and posts it in Ledgerline when it arrives.
What does the clerk record in the Rec Log when resolving a disputed item?
The clerk records the outcome of the dispute, either supplier correct or credit note requested, and the date it was resolved, against that supplier line in the Rec Log.
What observable result tells you a supplier’s reconciliation is complete?
The clerk marks the supplier Done in the Rec Log. For any reconciliation with a difference over 500 pounds, I must also have reviewed it and put my initials in cell B2 of the supplier tab.
What does your review of reconciliations over £500 check?

I check that each difference has been classified correctly, that the follow-up action has been taken and logged in the Rec Log, and that the totals on the tab agree to the statement and the open-items report. Then I initial B2.
Where are differences under £50 noted?
They are noted in a comment line on that supplier's tab in the Statement Rec Template workbook, with the total difference amount. They are not logged anywhere else.
What does this reconciliation help the finance team accomplish?
It confirms that what each supplier says we owe matches our payables ledger, so missing invoices and duplicate payments are found before month-end.
How is a supplier’s total difference of exactly £50 handled?
A total of exactly 50 pounds is treated as a larger difference, so it is classified and followed up. Only totals strictly under 50 pounds are ignored.
What happens after the supplier sends the requested invoice copy?

The clerk passes the invoice copy to the accounts payable team to be entered into Ledgerline, then updates the Rec Log line for that supplier. Until it is entered, it stays on the missing-invoice list used for month-end accruals.
What does the clerk record in the Rec Log once the invoice has been entered in Ledgerline?
The clerk marks that missing-invoice line as resolved in the Rec Log and records the date the invoice was entered.
What do you do after the clerk emails you about a duplicate?
I block the duplicate in Ledgerline within one business day so it cannot be paid.
What do you record in the Rec Log after blocking a duplicate?
I record nothing myself. I reply to the clerk by email that the block is in place, and the clerk marks the duplicate line as blocked in the Rec Log with the date.
After you block a duplicate and the clerk records it as blocked, what happens to that item in the reconciliation?
The item is treated as resolved and nothing further happens to it. The clerk can then mark the supplier Done once all its other differences are closed.
Who is accountable for the overall reconciliation result?
The finance manager, Dana Whitlock, is accountable for the process. I own the day-to-day running of it.
Who uses the completed reconciliation result next?
The accountant in the month-end accruals process uses the missing-invoice list. Internal audit also samples 10 reconciliations each quarter.
About how many supplier statements does the clerk usually reconcile in a week?
About 60 suppliers a week, and about 80 in the first week of the month. Around 6 a week have a difference over 50 pounds.
What most often prevents a supplier reconciliation from being completed on time?
Buyers replying slowly to disputes is the most common cause. The manual copying of statement lines into the workbook, about 10 minutes per supplier, also eats time.
Does this reconciliation cover all suppliers, or only a particular group?
It covers all trade suppliers of Northfield Tools Ltd, one UK legal entity, that send a statement that week. Employee expenses and intercompany are out of scope.
What happens to the disputed item when the buyer replies within five business days?

The buyer tells the clerk whether the supplier is right or we are, and the item then follows the same outcome as before: nothing changes if the supplier is right, or a credit note is requested if we are right. The clerk records it in the Rec Log.
What starts the buyer’s five-business-day reply period?
It starts on the day the clerk emails the dispute to the buyer.
When does your review of reconciliations over £500 happen relative to the clerk marking the supplier Done?
I review and initial before the clerk marks the supplier Done, normally within the Tuesday or Wednesday of that week, so it is all finished by Wednesday 17:00.
What happens if your review finds an error?
I send the reconciliation back to the clerk by email with what is wrong, the clerk corrects the tab, and I review it again before initialling.
What happens if a reconciliation error or delay is not caught before month-end?
We risk duplicate payments, such as the 4,200 pound one caught last year, and unrecorded liabilities at month-end because missing invoices are not accrued.
Where does the clerk note a payment in transit?
The clerk notes it on that supplier's tab in the workbook, using the weekly payment run report from Treasury to spot it. It is not logged elsewhere.
How does the set of statements you reconcile relate to those received in the mailbox during the previous week?
They are the same set: every statement that arrived in the mailbox in the previous week is reconciled. Statements arriving after Friday 17:00 go into the next week.
What happens if the supplier does not send the requested invoice copy?
The clerk chases the supplier by email once more the following week. The line stays open on the missing-invoice list, which the month-end accountant accrues, until the invoice arrives.
What is the basis for the £50 threshold?
The 50 pound and 500 pound limits both come from the procedure AP-07 Statement Reconciliation. The Wednesday deadline was set by the finance manager.
Is AP-07 the procedure you follow for this reconciliation today?
Yes, it is the procedure we follow. It is a two-page document on the finance shared drive, last updated in March, and it has not been reviewed in this interview.
What is your role in this reconciliation?
I am the AP supervisor. I own the day-to-day, block duplicates in Ledgerline, chase buyers on disputes, and review and initial reconciliations over 500 pounds. That takes about 1 hour a week.
How does the clerk decide whether a statement line matches an open item?
The clerk matches on supplier invoice number and amount. A line with no matching invoice number, or a different amount, counts as a difference.
How does the clerk calculate the supplier’s total difference from the individual unmatched or amount-different lines?
The clerk adds up the absolute value of each difference, ignoring whether it is over or under, so that differences do not cancel out. The sum is shown at the foot of the supplier tab.
Does the Statement Rec Template workbook calculate anything beyond the total difference?
No. The workbook only totals the differences per supplier and lists the line classifications. There are no other calculations in it.
After the credit note is posted in Ledgerline, what does the clerk record in the Rec Log?
The clerk marks the disputed line as resolved in the Rec Log, with the credit note number and the date it was posted.
How does the clerk coordinate having the statement and open-items report ready for comparison?
There is no coordination needed. The clerk does both themselves: saves the statement PDF to the weekly folder, then exports the open-items report for that supplier, and compares them in the workbook.
After your one chase, how does the disputed item get to Dana?
If the buyer still has not replied after my one chase, I forward the dispute email thread to Dana Whitlock by email and copy the clerk.
What information does Dana use to decide the outcome of a disputed item?
She uses the statement line, the invoice or purchase order, the Ledgerline record, and the buyer and supplier correspondence in the email thread.
What happens if a requested credit note does not arrive?
The clerk chases the supplier by email weekly, and the line stays open in the Rec Log. If it is still outstanding after a month I raise it with Dana.
What does Dana do when you raise a credit note that is still outstanding after a month?
Dana contacts the supplier's account manager directly to get the credit note issued, and tells me when it is done.
What happens if the buyer replies after you have escalated the dispute to Dana?
I forward the buyer's reply to Dana, who takes it into account when she decides the outcome.
How does the clerk let you know a corrected tab is ready for re-review?
Your account so far is saved. Still open: Variations and conditions, Data & systems, Volume & effort. You can create a draft from what is here, or keep answering.

map.title: Supplier statement reconciliation

steps.title: Monday scheduled start
steps.description: The work starts every Monday at 9:00.

steps.title: Download supplier statements
steps.description: The clerk downloads every statement received in the mailbox during the previous week. Statements arriving after Friday 17:00 go into the next week. Scope covers Northfield Tools Ltd trade suppliers that send a statement; employee expenses and intercompany are excluded.

steps.title: Save statement PDFs
steps.description: The clerk saves each statement PDF in Statements/YYYY-WW on the shared drive.

steps.title: Export supplier open-items report
steps.description: The clerk exports the open-items report for the supplier from Ledgerline.

steps.title: Compare statement and open items
steps.description: The clerk compares statement lines with open items on one tab per supplier, matching invoice number and amount. A missing matching number or different amount is a difference. The total is the sum of absolute differences; the workbook totals the differences and lists classifications, with no other calculations.

steps.title: Is the total difference under £50?
steps.description: Totals strictly under £50 are noted and ignored. Exactly £50 is classified for follow-up. The participant attributes the limit to AP-07; the procedure has not been reviewed.

steps.title: Note and ignore difference
steps.description: A supplier’s total difference under £50 is noted in a comment line on the supplier’s tab and ignored. It is not logged elsewhere.

steps.title: Classify larger differences
steps.description: For a supplier total of £50 or more, the clerk classifies each difference as missing invoice, payment in transit, duplicate or disputed. The workbook lists the classifications. The participant attributes the £50 limit to AP-07, which has not been reviewed.

steps.title: Request missing invoice copy
steps.description: The clerk emails the supplier asking for a copy of the missing invoice.

steps.title: Log missing invoice request
steps.description: The clerk logs the missing invoice request in the Rec Log sheet.

steps.title: Email duplicate to supervisor
steps.description: For a duplicate, the clerk emails the AP supervisor the same day.

steps.title: Note payment in transit
steps.description: The clerk uses Treasury’s weekly payment run report to spot a payment in transit and notes it on the supplier’s tab. It needs no further action and is not logged elsewhere.

steps.title: Email dispute to buyer
steps.description: The clerk emails the dispute to the buyer who placed the order.

steps.title: Wait for buyer reply
steps.description: The buyer has five business days to reply, starting on the day the clerk emails the dispute.

steps.title: Chase buyer once
steps.description: If the buyer does not reply within five business days, the AP supervisor chases them once. If there is still no reply after the chase, the supervisor forwards the dispute to the finance manager.

steps.title: Forward dispute to finance manager
steps.description: If the buyer still has not replied after the one chase, the AP supervisor forwards the dispute email thread to finance manager Dana Whitlock and copies the clerk. The timing after the chase is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Decide dispute outcome
steps.description: The finance manager decides the outcome with the buyer and supplier, using the statement line, invoice or purchase order, Ledgerline record and email correspondence. She takes a forwarded late buyer reply into account.

steps.title: Communicate dispute outcome
steps.description: The finance manager tells the AP supervisor and clerk the dispute outcome.

steps.title: Record dispute outcome
steps.description: The clerk records the outcome of the dispute, either supplier correct or credit note requested, and the date it was resolved, against that supplier line in the Rec Log.

steps.title: Communicate buyer dispute outcome
steps.description: The buyer tells the clerk whether the supplier or the organization is right. The clerk records the outcome or requests a credit note, as applicable.

steps.title: Post received credit note
steps.description: The clerk posts the credit note in Ledgerline when it arrives.

steps.title: Request supplier credit note
steps.description: If the organization is right, the clerk asks the supplier for a credit note. This applies to both the finance manager's outcome and a timely buyer outcome.

steps.title: Mark supplier Done
steps.description: The clerk marks the supplier Done. After a duplicate is blocked and recorded, all other differences must also be closed; for a difference over £500, the AP supervisor's review and initials must precede Done. Conditions on other routes are UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Supplier reconciliation complete
steps.system: Rec Log and Statement Rec Template workbook
steps.description: The supplier is marked Done in the Rec Log. For a difference over £500, the AP supervisor must also have reviewed the reconciliation and initialled the supplier tab. Internal audit samples 10 reconciliations each quarter; whether the sample is limited to completed reconciliations is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Pass invoice copy to AP
steps.description: The clerk passes the supplier’s invoice copy to accounts payable for entry into Ledgerline. Until entry, it remains on the missing-invoice list used by the accountant for month-end accruals.

steps.title: Enter invoice in Ledgerline
steps.description: The invoice copy is passed to accounts payable for entry into Ledgerline. The item remains on the missing-invoice list until entry.

steps.title: Update missing-invoice log
steps.description: After passing the invoice copy to accounts payable, the clerk updates the supplier's Rec Log line. The content of the update is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Review reconciliation
steps.system: Statement Rec Template workbook and Rec Log
steps.description: For a difference over £500, the AP supervisor checks classifications, follow-up and logging, and agreement of tab totals to the statement and the open-items report. If satisfactory, the supervisor initials B2; errors are returned for correction and re-review. AP-07 is the reported source of the limit but has not been reviewed.

steps.title: Confirm duplicate block
steps.description: The AP supervisor replies to the clerk by email that the block is in place. The supervisor does not record it in the Rec Log.

steps.title: Record duplicate block
steps.description: The clerk marks the duplicate line blocked and records the date. The item is then treated as resolved, with no further action on it.

steps.title: Block duplicate in Ledgerline
steps.description: The AP supervisor blocks the duplicate within one business day so it cannot be paid, then confirms the block to the clerk.

steps.title: Resolve missing-invoice line
steps.description: Once the invoice has been entered, the clerk marks the missing-invoice line as resolved in the Rec Log and records the date the invoice was entered.

steps.title: Return reconciliation for correction
steps.description: The AP supervisor emails the reconciliation back to the clerk, explaining what is wrong.

steps.title: Correct supplier tab
steps.description: The clerk corrects the tab following the review error; the AP supervisor reviews it again before initialling.

steps.title: Chase missing invoice
steps.description: If the requested invoice copy has not arrived, the clerk emails the supplier once more the following week. The line stays open on the missing-invoice list until the invoice arrives; the month-end accountant accrues it.

steps.title: Record posted credit resolution
steps.description: After posting the credit note, the clerk marks the disputed line resolved and records the credit note identifier and posting date.

steps.title: Chase outstanding credit note
steps.description: If the requested credit note has not arrived, the clerk chases the supplier by email weekly. The disputed line stays open in the Rec Log.

steps.title: Raise outstanding credit note
steps.description: If the credit note is still outstanding after a month, the AP supervisor raises it with finance manager Dana Whitlock.

steps.title: Contact supplier account manager
steps.description: Dana contacts the supplier's account manager directly to get the outstanding credit note issued and tells the AP supervisor when it is done.

steps.title: Forward late buyer reply
steps.description: If the buyer replies after escalation, the supervisor forwards the reply to Dana for consideration in her decision.

draft.title: DRAFT — Supplier statement reconciliation
draft.overview: Current-practice account for Northfield Tools Ltd, pending process-owner review. The AP clerk reconciles weekly supplier statements; the AP supervisor manages daily work and the finance manager is accountable. Some closure and exception handoffs remain UNKNOWN.
draft.trigger: Every Monday at 9:00 the AP clerk downloads the prior week's statements from the shared mailbox. Statements arriving after Friday 17:00 move to the following week.
inputs: Supplier statements from the shared mailbox
Supplier open-items reports exported from Ledgerline
Invoice or purchase order and buyer and supplier correspondence for escalated disputes
outputs: Supplier reconciliation in the Statement Rec Template
Supplier Done status and difference records in the Rec Log
Missing-invoice list used for month-end accruals
Duplicate blocks and posted credit notes in Ledgerline, where applicable
exceptions: A missing invoice not received is chased once more the following week and remains on the missing-invoice list for accrual until it arrives.
An unanswered dispute is chased once after five business days and forwarded to the finance manager if still unanswered. A later buyer reply is forwarded to her.
An outstanding credit note is chased weekly and escalated after a month; the line remains open.
Review errors are emailed back for correction and re-review.
controls: The clerk matches supplier invoice number and amount and totals absolute differences.
Totals under £50 are noted and ignored; exactly £50 is classified and followed up.
The AP supervisor blocks duplicates in Ledgerline within one business day to prevent payment.
For a difference over £500, the supervisor checks classification, logged follow-up and agreement of totals, and initials B2 before Done.
Internal audit samples 10 reconciliations quarterly; the sample's exact scope is UNKNOWN.

The account establishes Done and the duplicate-specific closure condition, but does not explain how several other difference routes reach supplier-level completion. Those known fragments remain disconnected from Done.

Review and initialling over £500 and, where a duplicate is present, closure of the other differences are both required before Done. Their order and coordination are UNKNOWN; neither prerequisite is sufficient alone.
The timing of the dispute outcome and resolved-date recording on the credit-note route is unclear relative to posting; premature closure cannot be assumed.
The over-£500 review is required before Done, but its readiness and placement relative to handling each difference are not fully described. Its incoming route is therefore unresolved.
The missing-invoice request is logged and the supplier is chased if the copy does not arrive, but the account does not make completion of the log entry the handoff that starts the chase.

The finance manager contacts the supplier's account manager and tells the supervisor when it is done. What 'done' means and the handoff on issuance or receipt remain unclear; weekly chasing remains a reported duty while the credit note is outstanding.

steps.title: Monday scheduled start
steps.description: The weekly work starts on Monday at 9:00.

steps.title: Download supplier statements
steps.description: Download all trade-supplier statements received in the previous week's set. Statements arriving after Friday 17:00 go into the next week. Scope is Northfield Tools Ltd; employee expenses and intercompany are excluded.

steps.title: Save statement PDFs
steps.description: Save each statement PDF in Statements/YYYY-WW on the shared drive.

steps.title: Export supplier open-items report
steps.description: Export the open-items report for the supplier from Ledgerline after saving the statement.

steps.title: Compare statement and open items
steps.description: Manually copy statement lines into the workbook, using one tab per supplier, and compare them with the open-items report. Match on supplier invoice number and amount; a missing matching number or different amount is a difference. Add the absolute values of differences so over- and under-differences do not cancel. The workbook shows the total at the foot of the tab and lists classifications; it performs no other calculations. Copying takes about 10 minutes per supplier, according to the participant.

steps.title: Is the total under £50?
steps.description: A total strictly under £50 is noted and ignored. Exactly £50 follows the classification route. The participant attributes the limit to AP-07, which was not reviewed.

steps.title: Note and ignore difference
steps.description: Note a total under £50 in a comment line on the supplier tab and ignore it. It is not logged elsewhere.

steps.title: Classify larger differences
steps.description: For a supplier total of £50 or more, classify each difference as missing invoice, payment in transit, duplicate or disputed. The workbook lists classifications.

steps.title: Request missing invoice copy
steps.description: Email the supplier the same day to request a copy of a missing invoice.

steps.title: Log missing invoice request
steps.description: Log the missing-invoice request in the Rec Log.

steps.title: Email duplicate to supervisor
steps.description: Email the AP supervisor about a duplicate the same day.

steps.title: Note payment in transit
steps.description: Use Treasury's weekly payment run report to spot a payment in transit and note it on the supplier tab. No further action is needed and it is not logged elsewhere.

steps.title: Email dispute to buyer
steps.description: Email the disputed item to the buyer who placed the order. The five-business-day reply period starts on the email day.

steps.title: Wait for buyer reply
steps.description: The buyer has five business days to reply, starting on the day the clerk emails the dispute.

steps.title: Chase buyer once
steps.description: If the buyer has not replied within five business days, chase once. If there is still no reply, forward the thread to the finance manager.

steps.title: Forward dispute to finance manager
steps.description: If the buyer still has not replied after the chase, forward the dispute email thread to Dana Whitlock and copy the clerk. Timing after the chase is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Decide dispute outcome
steps.description: Decide the escalated dispute with the buyer and supplier, using the statement line, invoice or purchase order, Ledgerline record and correspondence. Take a forwarded late buyer reply into account when deciding.

steps.title: Communicate dispute outcome
steps.description: Tell the AP supervisor and clerk the dispute outcome.

steps.title: Record dispute outcome
steps.description: Record the dispute outcome as supplier correct or credit note requested, and record the date resolved against the supplier line. The timing of the resolved-date entry on the credit-note route is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Communicate buyer dispute outcome
steps.description: For a timely reply, tell the clerk whether the supplier or the company is right. Supplier correct means no change; company correct leads to a credit-note request.

steps.title: Post received credit note
steps.description: Post the supplier's credit note in Ledgerline when it arrives.

steps.title: Request supplier credit note
steps.description: If the company is right, ask the supplier for a credit note. This outcome applies to both a timely buyer reply and the finance manager's decision.

steps.title: Mark supplier Done
steps.description: Mark the supplier Done. For a duplicate, the blocked item is resolved and all other differences must be closed. For a difference over £500, the supervisor must review and initial before Done. Conditions for other routes remain UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Supplier reconciliation complete
steps.system: Rec Log and supplier workbook tab
steps.description: The supplier is marked Done; for a difference over £500 the supervisor has also reviewed and initialled the tab. Internal audit samples 10 reconciliations quarterly; whether only completed reconciliations are sampled is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Pass invoice copy to AP
steps.description: Pass the received invoice copy to accounts payable for entry into Ledgerline. It remains on the missing-invoice list until entry, for month-end accruals.

steps.title: Enter invoice in Ledgerline
steps.description: Enter the invoice copy in Ledgerline. The item remains on the missing-invoice list until entry.

steps.title: Update missing-invoice log
steps.description: After passing the invoice copy to AP, update the supplier's Rec Log line. The content of this update is UNKNOWN.

steps.title: Review reconciliation
steps.system: Statement Rec Template workbook and Rec Log
steps.description: For a difference over £500, check that each difference is classified correctly, follow-up has been taken and logged, and tab totals agree to the statement and open-items report. Initial B2 after the check; if an error is found, return it for correction and review again. Review and initials precede Done and are normally Tuesday or Wednesday; the finance manager set the Wednesday 17:00 finish deadline. AP-07 is the reported threshold source, not reviewed.

steps.title: Confirm duplicate block
steps.description: Reply to the clerk by email that the block is in place. The supervisor records nothing in the Rec Log.

steps.title: Record duplicate block
steps.description: Mark the duplicate line blocked and record the date. The item is treated as resolved and nothing further happens to it; the supplier can be marked Done once other differences are closed.

steps.title: Block duplicate in Ledgerline
steps.description: Block the duplicate within one business day so it cannot be paid, then confirm the block to the clerk.

steps.title: Resolve missing-invoice line
steps.description: Once the invoice is entered, mark the missing-invoice line resolved and record the invoice entry date.

steps.title: Return reconciliation for correction
steps.description: If review finds an error, email the reconciliation back to the clerk explaining what is wrong.

steps.title: Correct supplier tab
steps.description: Correct the tab following the review error. The supervisor reviews it again before initialling.

steps.title: Chase missing invoice
steps.description: If the copy has not arrived, email the supplier once more the following week. The line stays open on the missing-invoice list until arrival; the month-end accountant accrues it.

steps.title: Record posted credit resolution
steps.description: After posting the credit note, mark the disputed line resolved and record its credit-note identifier and posting date.

steps.title: Chase outstanding credit note
steps.description: Chase the supplier by email weekly while the credit note is outstanding; the line stays open in the Rec Log. The supervisor raises it with Dana if still outstanding after a month.

steps.title: Raise outstanding credit note
steps.description: If the credit note is still outstanding after a month, raise it with Dana Whitlock.

steps.title: Contact supplier account manager
steps.description: Contact the supplier's account manager directly to get the credit note issued and tell the supervisor when it is done. Coordination of issuance and receipt is UNKNOWN. The clerk's reported weekly chasing continues while the credit note remains outstanding.

steps.title: Forward late buyer reply
steps.description: If the buyer replies after escalation, forward the reply to Dana, who takes it into account when deciding the outcome.

topics.answer: Supplier statement reconciliation is the intake name. Other team, checklist or system names are UNKNOWN.
Confirm that each supplier's stated amount owed matches the payables ledger, finding missing invoices and duplicate payments before month-end.

Every Monday at 9:00 the AP clerk downloads the previous week's statements from the shared mailbox.
Statements arriving after Friday 17:00 go into the next week's set.
The reported completion deadline is Wednesday 17:00.
The work is initiated by trade suppliers' statements arriving in the ap-statements shared mailbox; the statements received in the previous week form the set for reconciliation.

The clerk marks the supplier Done in the Rec Log. For a difference over £500, the supervisor reviews and initials B2 before Done. A blocked and recorded duplicate is resolved, and the supplier can be marked Done once its other differences are closed. The reported deadline is Wednesday 17:00. Conditions and handoffs to Done for several other routes remain UNKNOWN.
Finance manager Dana Whitlock is accountable; the AP supervisor owns day-to-day running.

The clerk downloads and saves each statement PDF, exports supplier open items from Ledgerline and compares invoice number and amount in a supplier workbook tab. Absolute differences are totalled: under £50 is noted and ignored; £50 or more is classified. Missing invoices are requested and logged, then passed to AP for entry and resolved in the log; absent copies are chased the following week and stay on the accrual list. Duplicates go to the supervisor for a Ledgerline block and email confirmation, after which the clerk records the block. Payments in transit are noted using Treasury's report. Disputes go to the buyer; unanswered disputes are chased and escalated to Dana, while timely answers or Dana's decision determine whether nothing changes or a credit note is requested and posted. Outstanding credits are chased weekly and escalated after a month. The clerk records outcomes and marks Done; over £500 the supervisor reviews and initials first, returning errors for correction and re-review. Several routes' handoffs to Done, the review's readiness point and the timing of the credit-note outcome entry remain UNKNOWN.

The clerk matches invoice number and amount, totals absolute differences and classifies larger differences. The supervisor blocks duplicates to prevent payment and, over £500, checks classification, logged follow-up and agreement of totals to the statement and open-items report, then initials B2 before Done. Errors are returned by email for correction and re-review. Dana decides escalated disputes using the statement, invoice or purchase order, Ledgerline and correspondence. Internal audit samples 10 reconciliations quarterly. Review readiness, other approval or override arrangements, technical enforcement and the audit sample's exact scope are UNKNOWN.

Handling varies by total and difference class: under £50 is noted, £50 or more is classified, and over £500 receives supervisor review. Missing invoices, duplicates, payments in transit and disputes have different follow-up; outstanding invoice copies and credits have chase routes. Client, supplier or other structural differences and their source or effort are UNKNOWN.
The participant says slow buyer replies are the most common cause of late completion. Manually copying statement lines takes about 10 minutes per supplier.

Errors or delays risk duplicate payments and unrecorded month-end liabilities if missing invoices are not accrued. The participant cited a £4,200 duplicate payment caught last year; duplicate blocking is intended to prevent payment.

The work uses supplier PDFs, Ledgerline open-items reports, the Statement Rec Template, Rec Log, missing-invoice list and Treasury payment run report. AP-07 Statement Reconciliation is reportedly followed; it is a two-page document on the finance shared drive, last updated in March, and was not reviewed in the interview. Escalated disputes also use the statement line, invoice or purchase order, ledger record and correspondence. Locations and availability of the remaining materials are not fully established.

The work covers trade suppliers of Northfield Tools Ltd, one UK legal entity, that send a statement that week. Employee expenses and intercompany are out of scope. Whether this is local or general practice and its parent-process boundary are UNKNOWN.

The participant attributes the £50 and £500 limits to AP-07, which was not reviewed, and says the finance manager set the Wednesday deadline. Exactly £50 is classified; only totals strictly below it are ignored. The clerk matches invoice number and amount and sums absolute differences so signs do not cancel. Over £500, review and initials precede Done. Buyer reply time starts on the dispute email day; the Friday 17:00 cutoff determines the weekly set. Rule interpretation, conflict authority and calculation-logic ownership are UNKNOWN.

Treasury supplies the weekly payment run report. The clerk hands received invoice copies to AP for Ledgerline entry; the month-end accountant uses and accrues the missing-invoice list. Buyers and the finance manager resolve disputes, and internal audit samples reconciliations quarterly. The supervisor confirms duplicate blocks to the clerk and forwards escalated disputes and late replies to Dana. Readiness signals and the handoffs from several difference routes to supplier completion are UNKNOWN.

Statements come from the shared mailbox and PDFs are saved on the shared drive. Ledgerline supplies open items and holds duplicate blocks, invoice entries and posted credits. Statement lines are manually copied into the supplier workbook tab, which totals differences and lists classifications; the Rec Log records outcomes and Done. Treasury report storage and authoritative records are UNKNOWN.

The participant estimates about 60 suppliers weekly, rising to 80 in the first week of the month, and around six weekly with a difference over £50. Copying takes about 10 minutes per supplier; the supervisor estimates one hour weekly for their duties. Internal audit samples 10 reconciliations quarterly. Other exception rates and step effort are UNKNOWN.
